definitions.definition: The nature of awakening present in all beings without distinction of north and south, identical with the self-nature; seeing it is becoming buddha.
For Dōgen, 'whole being is buddha-nature' and impermanence itself is buddha-nature; not a seed or potential.
'All beings are originally buddhas', like ice that is water (Hakuin).

equivalents.note: The Chinese rendering of buddhadhātu in the Nirvāṇa-sūtra, which Chan inherits.
Chan uses both, but seldom the embryo image.

definitions.definition: The originally pure, unborn, complete and unmoving nature of one's own mind that produces all dharmas (Huineng's awakening); delusion and awakening are its states.
One's own nature, the Dharma body, recognised in sudden awakening (Jinul).

equivalents.note: Same Chinese word as the svabhāva that Madhyamaka refutes; in the Platform Sūtra it names the empty, originally pure nature of mind, not an inherent own-being of dharmas; Madhyamaka would object to any reading of zixing as svabhāva.

definitions.definition: One's own original mind; without recognising it, study of the Dharma is useless (Hongren to Huineng).
One's original face 'before thinking good or evil' (Huineng to Huiming); a pointer to the self-nature.
The empty and calm numinous knowing mind is one's original face (Jinul).
A standard pointer and kōan ('your original face before your parents were born').

term: benlai wu yi wu (originally not a single thing)
literal: originally there is not one thing

definitions.definition: Third line of Huineng's verse in the Zongbao Platform Sūtra, denying anything to be wiped clean.
In Chan the word for the ultimate itself — 'this very mind is buddha' — as well as for deluded mind; which is meant depends on context.
The formless mind-dharma pervading the ten directions, functioning as seeing, hearing and acting (Linji).
The one mind that buddhas and beings are; there is no other dharma (Huangbo).
The source (zong) taken by Yongming Yanshou to harmonise Chan and the teachings.
The true mind, like space, neither cut off nor changing, as opposed to the provisional body and deluded mind (Jinul).

term: kongji lingzhi (empty and calm, numinous awareness)

definitions.definition: The empty, quiescent mind whose numinous knowing is never obscured — one's true nature; 'the one word knowing is the gate of all wonders' (Zongmi on Heze).
One's original face and the Dharma-seal of the buddhas; the questioner himself (Jinul).

equivalents.note: Both name an unobscured knowing nature of mind; the Chan term comes through Zongmi's Heze and Huayan synthesis, not from the Indian luminous-mind passages.

definitions.definition: The numinous light that shines alone, free of senses and objects (Baizhang's style as proclaimed by Guling).
The bright and pure source whose branches flow in the dark (Cantongqi).

term: wuwei zhenren (true person of no rank)

definitions.definition: The true person without rank going in and out of the gates of the face; not to be reified ('a dried shit-stick') (Linji).

term: wuyi daoren (person of the Way who depends on nothing)

definitions.definition: The one listening to the Dharma who relies on nothing, the mother of all buddhas (Linji).
The unborn buddha-mind everyone has from their parents, which illuminates everything without intention (Bankei).

term: jixin jifo (this very mind is buddha)

definitions.definition: Mazu's teaching that the mind right now is buddha, later complemented by 'neither mind nor buddha'.
Explained in the Platform Sūtra as 'the previous thought not arising is mind, the next thought not ceasing is buddha'.
Dōgen rejects reading it as the Śreṇika view of an eternal knowing mind (Sokushin zebutsu).
Mazu's negating counterpart to 'this very mind is buddha' (Wumenguan case 33).
The mind without contrivance, right and wrong, grasping and rejecting — 'the ordinary mind is the Way' (Mazu, Nanquan).
The state of the one who has stopped seeking: ordinary, with nothing to do — 'the noble person is the one with nothing to do' (Linji).

term: suichu zuozhu, lichu jiezhen (be master wherever you are; wherever you stand is true)

definitions.definition: Linji's maxim of autonomy: not swayed by circumstances.
The insight Linji demands: no longer seeking outside, one is not stained by birth and death.
Transcription of dhyāna; in the Platform Sūtra 'inwardly seeing the unmoving self-nature'; also the name of the school.

equivalents.note: Chan transcribes dhyāna, but as a school name it means the lineage of the buddha-mind, and the Platform Sūtra redefines it as seeing the self-nature rather than a meditative absorption.

definitions.definition: Redefined in the Platform Sūtra: not attaching to mind or purity nor mere immobility; 'sitting' is thoughts not arising toward objects, 'meditation' is seeing the unmoving self-nature.
Just sitting as the enactment of buddhahood; 'not learning meditation but the Dharma gate of ease and joy' (Dōgen).
The seat of kōan introspection and of samādhi-power (jōriki).
Sitting wholeheartedly without seeking a further goal or object; taught by Rujing to Dōgen ('only just sit') and by Dōgen as practice-realization.
Yaoshan's answer: 'thinking of not-thinking — non-thinking'.
'The essential art of zazen' (Fukanzazengi).

term: shushō ittō (oneness of practice and realization)

definitions.definition: Practice is practice-in-realization, so even a beginner's practice is the whole of original realization (Bendōwa).

term: shinjin datsuraku (body and mind dropping off)

definitions.definition: Dōgen's account of Rujing's teaching and of his own awakening; in Genjōkōan, the dropping off of the body and mind of oneself and others when verified by the myriad dharmas.

notes: Rujing's own record has 心塵脫落 (the dust of mind drops off), homophonous in Japanese (tea:rujing-yulu:130c19).

definitions.definition: Reality presenting itself as the fundamental 'case'; title of Dōgen's essay.
Time is being and being is time; each moment abides in its dharma-position (Dōgen).
An encounter, saying or story of the ancients taken up as a 'case' for commentary and contemplation; Wumen calls them 'tiles to knock on the gate'.
The central device of training, worked on in private interview under a teacher within a graded curriculum.
The key word of a case (e.g. 'wu') held with doubt at all times until it shatters (Dahui).
The 'live word' (hwalgu) of ganhwa Seon, the shortcut gate (Jinul, Hyujeong).

term: kanhua Chan / ganhwa Seon (Chan of observing the phrase)

definitions.definition: Dahui's method of concentrating doubt on a huatou.
The mainstream practice of the Jogye order from Jinul and Hyesim onward.
Silence in which words are forgotten and clear illumination appears; the two must not lose each other (Hongzhi).
'Heretical silent-illumination Chan' in Dahui's criticism — sitting like dead ash.
The doubt aroused by the huatou which must be broken for awakening; 'great doubt, great awakening'.
Doubt involving the whole body — 'with your 360 bones and 84,000 pores raise a mass of doubt' (Wumen).
One of the three essentials with great faith and great determination (Gaofeng).
The decisive state of kōan practice described by Hakuin as being frozen in a sheet of ice before breaking through.
Zhaozhou's answer to 'does a dog have buddha-nature?', used as the first barrier; not to be taken as nothingness or as the 'no' of being and non-being.
Hakuin's kōan 'the sound of one hand'.
Bodhidharma's practice of 'abiding firmly in wall-gazing' in entry by principle; later understood as his nine years facing the wall.

term: liru and xingru (entry by principle, entry by practice)

definitions.definition: The two entrances of Bodhidharma's treatise.
Guarding the original true mind, the root of nirvāṇa (Hongren).
Daoxin's practice of guarding the one without moving (Lengqie shizi ji).
Northern-school practices of contemplating the mind and its purity, as reported and criticised by the Southern school.
Northern-school key term (from the Awakening of Faith) for the mind free of thoughts as the essence of awakening (Dasheng wusheng fangbian men).
The tenet of the Platform Sūtra: being amid thoughts yet not thinking, the mind not stained by objects; not a blank absence of thought.
The tenet of Shenhui's teaching.
Musang's 'no thinking' = samādhi.
For Wuzhu, no-thought includes precepts, samādhi and wisdom and replaces all ritual.

equivalents.note: Both mean the absence of conceptual thought, but the Platform Sūtra insists no-thought is thought of suchness, not a cessation of thought; Advaita and Yogācāra uses of nirvikalpa have different bases.

definitions.definition: The substance of the teaching: being amid forms yet free of forms; also the 'formless' precepts, repentance and verse.
The root of the teaching and the original nature of people: moment after moment not abiding in any dharma; from the Diamond Sūtra's 'produce a mind that abides nowhere'.
Takuan's mind that does not stop anywhere.

equivalents.note: The Diamond Sūtra's apratiṣṭhitaṃ cittam, which Huineng's awakening line renders.

term: ying wu suo zhu er sheng qi xin (produce a mind that abides nowhere)

definitions.definition: The Diamond Sūtra line at which Huineng awoke.
The state free of all mind of seeking and discriminating; 'only be without mind and that is the ultimate' (Huangbo).
Practised through ten methods of stopping deluded mind (Jinsim jikseol).
Directly seeing one's own nature at the words, the aim of Hongren's test and Huineng's teaching.
The breakthrough awakening of kōan practice, to be followed by post-awakening training.

term: jianxing chengfo (seeing the nature and becoming buddha)

definitions.definition: Last phrase of the four-line self-description; also used in the Platform Sūtra.
'Take awakening as the standard' (Dahui), against teachers who deny awakening.
Satori: awakening, used interchangeably with kenshō or for deeper realizations.
Awakening all at once to the self-nature; the Platform Sūtra says the Dharma has no sudden or gradual, only people are sharp or dull.
Recognising in one turning of the light that one's own nature is buddha (Jinul).
Cultivation after sudden awakening that gradually removes habit energies (Jinul, after Zongmi and Guishan).
Purifying beginningless habit energies after sudden awakening to principle (Guishan).
'Sudden awakening, sudden cultivation, without gradual steps' (Platform Sūtra, Zongbao).
Seongcheol's 'sudden awakening, sudden cultivation' (dono donsu) as the only true awakening.
Beginningless habitual tendencies that remain after sudden awakening and are removed gradually.

term: fanzhao / huiguang fanzhao (turning the light around)

definitions.definition: Turning awareness back upon its source; 'if you turn back the light, the secret is on your side' (Huineng to Huiming).
Linji: 'turn your light around right at the words and seek nothing else'.
Jinul's central practice of tracing back the radiance to the numinous awareness.
Samādhi and prajñā as one substance, lamp and light; their equal study.
The content of gradual cultivation: calm yet always knowing, knowing yet always calm (Jinul).
Pair used to relate samādhi (substance) and prajñā (function), suchness and thought.
Jinul: samādhi is substance, prajñā function, of the self-nature.
Balance of alertness and calm: calm without alertness is dullness, alertness without calm is scattered thought (Yongjia).
Jinul's seongjeok deungji; sequential use is the gradual method of inferior faculties.
The blank state of sitting with an empty mind thinking nothing, which the Platform Sūtra rejects.
Always practising a straight mind in all activities, not sitting motionless (Platform Sūtra).
Daoxin's samādhi of one practice drawn from the Wenshu shuo bore jing (Lengqie shizi ji).
Precepts, samādhi and wisdom: Shenxiu's version (not doing evil, doing good, purifying the mind) versus Huineng's 'three trainings of the self-nature'.
Musang's no-remembering, no-thinking, no-forgetting.
The Dharma, reward and transformation bodies found in one's own nature (Platform Sūtra).
Three kinds of light in one's own thought (Linji).

term: zixing zidu (saving oneself by the self-nature)

definitions.definition: The inward meaning of the four vows: the deluded beings of one's own mind are saved by one's own prajñā.
The previous thought attached to objects is affliction, the next thought free of objects is bodhi.
The discriminating preference that alone obstructs the supreme Way (Xinxin ming).
Conceptual understanding mistaken for awakening; Huineng calls Shenhui 'a follower of intellectual understanding' (Zongbao).
Seongcheol classes Jinul's understanding-awakening under this head.
The teacher who shows the way to see the nature, needed by those who cannot awaken themselves; Huineng also addresses his audience as 'good friends'.

term: shengsi shida (birth and death is the great matter)

definitions.definition: The urgency that motivates practice (Hongren; Yongjia).

term: yi xin chuan xin (transmission from mind to mind)

definitions.definition: The Dharma transmitted mind to mind, making each awaken for himself, while the robe was only a token (Hongren in the Platform Sūtra).

term: zhengfayanzang (treasury of the true Dharma eye)

definitions.definition: What the Buddha entrusted to Mahākāśyapa in the flower sermon; also a title (Dahui; Dōgen).

term: jiaowai biechuan (a special transmission outside the teachings)

definitions.definition: First line of the four-line self-description; in the flower-sermon account.

term: buli wenzi (not established on words and letters)

definitions.definition: Second line of the four-line self-description; the Platform Sūtra warns that even 'not establishing' is words.

term: zhizhi renxin (pointing directly at the human mind)

definitions.definition: Third line of the four-line self-description.
Linji's shout, with four functions (vajra sword, crouching lion, probing pole, not a shout).
The teacher's staff used to strike, associated with Deshan ('thirty blows') and Linji.
Taking away person and/or environment according to the student.
Each phrase contains three mysterious gates, each gate three essentials (Linji); later glossed as mystery in the substance, in the phrase, and in the mystery.
The four guest-host relations between teacher and student.
Caodong's own guest-host scheme, distinct from Linji's.
The four relations of illumination and function.

term: zheng and pian (the real and the apparent)

definitions.definition: The real (principle, emptiness, lord) and the apparent (phenomena, form, minister), whose interplay is the five ranks.
Things interfuse and do not interfuse, yet each abides in its place (Cantongqi).
Dongshan's leaks of view, feeling and words.
Circles and figures used as teaching devices, said to derive from Nanyang Huizhong through Danyuan to Yangshan.
Containing heaven and earth; cutting off the myriad streams; following the waves.

term: sharen dao, huoren jian (the sword that kills, the sword that gives life)

definitions.definition: The teacher's twofold function of cutting off delusion and restoring life (Yuanwu's pointer).

literal: Pure Land that is only mind

definitions.definition: 'As the mind is pure the buddha-land is pure': the Western Land is found in the purified mind (Platform Sūtra).
The field below the navel where breath and energy are gathered in Hakuin's naikan; contemplated as one's original face and Pure Land.

notes: Hakuin also uses kikai (氣海, 'sea of qi'); the term comes from Chinese medical and Daoist vocabulary (dantian).

definitions.definition: The teacher's formal confirmation that a student has completed training and may teach.
Confirmation by a living teacher, as Huineng confirmed Yongjia.
The dharma-transmission document listing the lineage, discussed in Dōgen's Shisho.
The lineage chart given at precept ordination or dharma transmission, linking the recipient to the Buddha.
The student's private meeting with the teacher to present understanding of the kōan.
A private interview for guidance.
Periods of intensive sitting, usually of seven days, in Japanese monasteries (e.g. rōhatsu sesshin in early December commemorating the Buddha's awakening).
A master's formal presentation of a text or kōan.
Brief comments inserted into a case (Biyan lu).
Phrases, often from the Zenrin kushū, that students present to show understanding of a kōan.
A phrase that turns delusion into awakening; e.g. Baizhang's 'not obscuring cause and effect'.
Slow or brisk walking meditation between periods of zazen.
Walking as practice ('walking too is Chan', Zhengdao ge).
Communal labour shared equally by high and low (Chanmen guishi, Chixiu qinggui).
Codes regulating Chan monastic life, traditionally from Baizhang; extant from 1103 (Chanyuan qinggui) and 1338 (Chixiu).
The illness Hakuin contracted from excessive striving — rising heat, cold legs, fear, exhaustion — cured by naikan.
Visions, lights, sounds and other unusual experiences arising in zazen, not to be clung to.
The stability developed through zazen, distinguished from kenshō and its later embodiment.
Training after kenshō, stressed by Hakuin and Tōrei.

literal: farewell to the world / bequeathed verse

definitions.definition: The verse composed by a master just before death, e.g. Huineng's last verse.

term: Rulai Chan and Zushi Chan (Tathāgata Chan and Patriarch Chan)

definitions.definition: Yangshan's distinction: Xiangyan had understood 'Tathāgata Chan' but not yet 'Patriarch Chan'; the latter came to mean the separate transmission beyond doctrinal meditation.
Zongmi used 'the pure Chan of the Tathāgata' for the highest Chan.
Jinul's normative path, following Zongmi.
Jinul's (after Zongmi) distinction between awakening in understanding, which precedes cultivation, and realization-awakening at its end; Seongcheol held only the latter to be Chan awakening.

term: three essentials of practice (great faith, great doubt, great determination)
native: 大信根 · 大疑情 · 大憤志

definitions.definition: Gaofeng Yuanmiao's three essentials for huatou practice.
Taught in the Seon'ga gwigam.
Bodhidharma's 'pacifying' of Huike's mind by showing it cannot be found; in Xu gaoseng zhuan, wall-gazing is 'pacifying the mind'.

term: wuqing shuofa (the insentient preach the Dharma)

definitions.definition: Nanyang Huizhong's teaching, taken up by Dongshan; heard only when one is free of the feelings of consciousness.
True merit is seeing the nature and equality in the Dharma body; building temples and giving are blessings (Platform Sūtra on Emperor Wu).
The five ranks of the real and the apparent (lord and minister) of Dongshan and Caoshan.
Rendered foxing; in Chan the self-nature seen in awakening, without distinction of region or status.
Transcribed chan; the Platform Sūtra redefines it as being free of forms outwardly (samādhi being inner non-confusion).
The monastic robe, regarded by Dōgen as the body and mind of the Buddha (Kesa kudoku).
Honorific for a Zen master authorised to teach.
A trainee monk who wanders like clouds and water.
The hall where monks sit, eat and sleep by seniority (Chanmen guishi).
A flat stick used in the meditation hall to strike the shoulders to rouse sitters.
The ninety-day training period derived from the rains retreat.
The abbot's room, likened to Vimalakīrti's chamber (Chanmen guishi).
Hall where the abbot preaches; Baizhang built no Buddha hall but only a Dharma hall.
Nōnin's claim of self-awakening, criticised by Eisai and contrary to the tradition's insistence on confirmation.
Chan's name for itself as against the 'teaching gate' (jiaomen) of the doctrinal schools.
The four texts of the Korean monastic curriculum: Dahui's Letters, Zongmi's Chan Preface, Jinul's Excerpts, Gaofeng's Essentials of Chan.
